picks.why: Chunkiest body and best fill of the frame, with a calm background and less glow than 1. Candidate 3 sits off-balance and looks slimmer. The red nose band is a minor extra.
Cleanest classic saucer read, with a smooth hull, simple lights and restrained metal. Candidate 1 has a heavy, toy-like rim band and candidate 2 sits off to the left.
Centred, with the ring wrapping the sphere correctly and the smallest blue crater, which is the extra all three share. Candidate 2 sits left and has a louder crater.
Larger in frame, like the real card's fill, with a solid rock and flames tucked behind it. Candidate 1 is smaller and its flame reads thinner.
Fewest invented parts: a plain shell, ear disc and neck ring. Candidate 1 adds vents and a table edge, and candidate 2 adds tabs on the collar.
Fills the frame with a chunky, believable wedge console and gauges, button rows and lever all legible. Candidates 2 and 3 are smaller, and 2 adds corner rivets.
Simplest rover, with a clean body, one windshield and a compact six-wheel stance like the real taxi's soft forms. Candidates 1 and 3 add orange stripes, and 1 reads as an SUV.
Plain cream tube with a gold rim and a simple tripod, balanced in the frame. Candidate 1 tapers too hard and tilts awkwardly, and 3 adds extra copper collars.
Well-proportioned dish on a simple round pedestal, instantly read and well framed. Candidate 3 has a darker, busier base and 1 has a blocky octagonal plinth.
Fewest invented extras: the dome interior stays simple, with only a light. Candidates 2 and 3 add furniture and plants, and 3 also adds yellow trim.
